title: Intact DNA purified from flow-sorted nuclei unlocks the potential of next-generation genome mapping and assembly in Solanum species
author: Gaiero, Šimková, et al.

Push the plugs into a polystyrene tube with 500 μL per plug of lysis buffer C (0.5 M EDTA, 1% N-lauroyl-sarcosine (Sigma Aldrich, L5000)). Add freshly prepared proteinase K (Sigma Aldrich, P6556) to reach a final concentration of 0.3 mg/mL (30 μL of stock solution per 1 mL). For the two washes, prepare 62 μL of stock solution per 1 mL of buffer. Weigh 62 μg and dilute in 62 μL of MQ (milli-Q, Millipore Corporation) water. Before weighing, let the proteinase K adapt to room temperature to avoid condensation on the powder. Add 30 μL for the first wash and keep the rest at 4 ℃ for the second wash.

Change for lysis buffer B (0.5 M EDTA, 1% N-lauroyl-sarcosine (Sigma Aldrich, L5000), 0.3 mg mL−1 proteinase K (Sigma Aldrich, P6556, pH 8.0) and incubate plugs for another 24 h under the same conditions.

steps.title: Germinate tomato seeds
steps.instruction: Place about 200 tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) seeds on humidified filter paper in Petri dishes and incubate for approximately 4 days.

steps.title: Prepare isolation buffer with β‑mercaptoethanol
steps.instruction: Make 1.5× isolation buffer (IB) containing 15 mM Tris, 10 mM EDTA, 130 mM KCl, 20 mM NaCl, 1 mM spermine, 1 mM spermidine and 0.1 % Triton X‑100, pH 9.4; just before use add 1.1 µL β‑mercaptoethanol per 1 mL of IB.

steps.title: Fix seedlings in formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Transfer seedlings to a 2 % formaldehyde solution (stock 36.5–38 % in H₂O, SIGMA F8775) prepared in Tris buffer (10 mM Tris, 10 mM EDTA, 100 mM NaCl, 0.1 % v/v Triton X‑100, pH 7.5). Incubate in a 4 °C water bath for 20 min, then wash three times in the same Tris buffer at 4 °C for 5 min each.

steps.title: Dissect root tips and chill
steps.instruction: On a glass Petri dish dissect 1–2 cm of tomato root tips, divide the material between two 5 mL polystyrene tubes each containing 1 mL ice‑cold 1.5× IB with β‑mercaptoethanol, and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue (or chop leaf tissue)
steps.instruction: For root tips: homogenize each tube using a Polytron PT1200 at 15 000 rpm for 13 s (adjust time/speed as needed for the species). For S. commersonii or S. etuberosum leaves: after fixation, rinse, place 0.5–1 g leaves in a glass Petri dish with 1 mL 1.5× IB and chop with a sharp razor blade until a soft green suspension of very small leaf pieces is obtained; then proceed as for the root‑tip homogenization.

steps.title: Filter homogenate to obtain nuclei
steps.instruction: Pass the crude homogenate sequentially through a 50 µm nylon mesh into a new polystyrene tube and then through a 25 µm nylon mesh (Silk & Progress, 130 T EXTRA) or, alternatively, through a Falcon® 40 µm cell strainer (Corning, product #352,340). Collect the filtered nuclei suspension up to a total volume of ~4 mL.

steps.title: Stain nuclei with DAPI and assess
steps.instruction: Add DAPI to the nuclei suspension to a final concentration of 2 µg mL⁻¹. Examine nuclei under a fluorescence microscope (appropriate excitation/emission filters) at 10× magnification; nuclei should be round, intact, and present at a density of 150–200 nuclei mm⁻².

steps.title: Keep nuclei on ice before sorting
steps.instruction: Maintain the stained nuclei suspension on ice until flow‑cytometric analysis and sorting.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei for plug preparation
steps.instruction: Transfer nuclei (400 000–500 000 per tube) to a centrifuge and spin at 500 g, 4 °C for 30 min. (Optional: perform fluorescence microscopy checkpoints before and after pelleting using 2 µg mL⁻¹ DAPI or 50 µg mL⁻¹ propidium iodide.)

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in residual supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant but retain ~15 µL with the pellet; gently resuspend the pelleted nuclei in this leftover supernatant.

steps.title: Warm nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Incubate the nuclei suspension at 52 °C for 3–5 min.

steps.title: Mix nuclei with low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Add 8.5 µL of 2 % low‑melting point (LMP) agarose (Bio‑Rad, 1613111) dissolved in 1× IB to the warmed nuclei suspension and mix.

steps.title: Pour mixture into plug molds
steps.instruction: Keep the mixture at 52 °C for an additional 5 min, then slowly dispense it into pre‑warmed plug molds (Bio‑Rad, 1703713) using a wide‑bore pipette tip.

steps.title: Solidify agarose plugs
steps.instruction: Place the plug molds at 4 °C for 10 min to allow solidification.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer C and proteinase K
steps.instruction: Transfer each solidified plug into a polystyrene tube containing 500 µL lysis buffer C (0.5 M EDTA, 1 % N‑lauroyl‑sarcosine, Sigma L5000). Add freshly prepared proteinase K (Sigma P6556) to a final concentration of 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ (30 µL of stock solution per 1 mL buffer). For the two subsequent washes, prepare a proteinase K stock of 62 µg mL⁻¹ by weighing 62 µg and dissolving in 62 µL milli‑Q water; add 30 µL of this stock to the first wash and keep the remainder at 4 °C for the second wash.

steps.title: Incubate plugs in buffer C
steps.instruction: Incubate the plugs at 37 °C for 24 h with gentle shaking at 50 rpm, positioning the tubes almost horizontally.

steps.title: Treat plugs with lysis buffer B
steps.instruction: Replace buffer C with lysis buffer B (0.5 M EDTA, 1 % N‑lauroyl‑sarcosine, 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ proteinase K, Sigma P6556, pH 8.0) and incubate for a further 24 h under the same temperature, shaking, and orientation conditions.

steps.title: Rinse and store plugs in ET buffer
steps.instruction: After the second proteinase K treatment, rinse the plugs and store them in ET buffer (1 mM Tris, 50 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality by PFGE
steps.instruction: Evaluate the high‑molecular‑weight DNA in the plugs using pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis (e.g., CHEF‑DR II system, Bio‑Rad or BluePippin, Sage Science) according to standard PFGE protocols.

steps.title: Proceed to downstream labeling
steps.instruction: Follow the standard BioNano Genomics protocol for RNAse treatment, DNA release, and labeling of the plugs.
